summary:
Bullpen is the category to lean on across the board today — R1, R2, and R3 all show bullpen at 100-90 (53%) over the last 14 days with a 3W streak on all three ratings, well above their season baselines (49-51%). That consistency across every rating suggests the model's bullpen inputs are reading current form accurately right now. Meanwhile SP is the fade: R1 and R2 sit at 86-104 (45%) over 14 days, and R3's SP cell is flagged COLD at -5.2pts, sliding from a 51% season mark to 46% recently. Runs is also shaky for R2, on a 4L streak and down to 47% over the last two weeks from a 52% season baseline. If you're stacking categories, trends+runs remains the best agreement combo at 54.7% (232-192, n=424), with trends+bullpen right behind at 53.9% — worth prioritizing trends-backed bullpen plays over anything leaning on SP right now.

Strong-play units are bleeding short-term across all three ratings: R1 is -15.0u over the last 7 days and -10.0u over 14, R2 is -14.0u/-12.0u, and R3 is -12.0u/-13.0u — a rough stretch model-wide, though all three retain solidly profitable season marks (R1 +12.0u, R2 +13.0u, R3 +23.0u), so this reads like a cold patch rather than a structural break. Team trust should guide sizing while the model resets: TBR strong plays are elite at 18-5 (78%, +22.0u), and LAD strong plays are money at 14-2 (88%, +17.0u) — both are green lights when the model likes them. BOS (71%, n=38) and CHC (70%, n=27) are similarly strong on straight picks. Flip side — HOU is the team to avoid on strong plays, going 3-8 (27%, -8.0u) despite a respectable overall record when picked. Bottom line for today: trust bullpen-graded, trends-backed picks, favor TBR/LAD/BOS when they surface, and treat any HOU or SP-heavy strong play with skepticism until the short-term skid breaks.
